sentences.text: Since the issues raised in these appeals are similar, they are being decided by a common judgment.
The facts of First Appeal No.2870 of 2023 is taken for the purpose of adjudication.
NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2870/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/02/2026 undefined 2.
These appeals are filed challenging the judgment dated 19.08.2017 and decree dated 28.08.2017 passed by the learned reference court in LAR No.515/2000 in group LAR Nos. 502/2000 to 516/2000

whereby, the learned reference court has awarded Rs.66/- per sq.mtr. for irrigated land and Rs.44/- per sq.mtr. for non-irrigated land for the land acquired by the village Bhapi, Taluka:
Tharad, District:
Banaskantha for the project of Narmada.

3. It is the case of the present appellant that land of the claimants were acquired for the above purpose by issuing the notification under section 4 dated 16.10.1998 and section 11 award came to be passed by the learned Special Land Acquisition Officer,
Narmada Project, Palanpur on 28.03.2000 where the price for the land under acquisition was fixed at the rate of Rs.1.40/- per sq.mtr. for non- irrigated land and Rs.2.10 per sq.mtr. for the irrigated land.
Being aggrieved and dissatisfied by the above award, the claimants have filed the application under section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act claiming the enhancement of the award.

The learned reference court, at the ends has passed NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2870/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/02/2026 undefined the judgment by determining the market value as aforesaid and the same is subject matter of challenge before this Court.
4. Heard learned advocate Mr.Tejas Satta with learned advocate Mr.Krushnakant Patel for the appellants and learned AGP Ms.Bhumi Gandhi for the respondent-State. 4.1.

Learned advocate Mr.Tejas Satta submits that learned reference court has committed error in relying on the decision rendered by this Court in First Appeal No.1138/2006 wherein for the adjoining village Vami, the market price at the rate of Rs.75/- per sq.mtr. is fixed.

Learned advocate Mr.Tejas Satta submits that in the said first appeal, the date of notification is 29.10.1999 however, in the subsequent decision of the same village, Vami this Court in First Appeal No.701/2017 where the date of notification under section 4 was 28.08.1997, fixed market value of the land at the rate of Rs.76/- per sq.mtr.

It is submitted by learned advocate Mr.Tejas Satta that claimants are entitled for the best price and as decision rendered by this Court in First Appeal No.701/2017 is NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2870/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/02/2026 undefined accepted by the State Authority,
the said decision is required to be applied herein and enhancement on the compensation accordingly is required to be given.

4.2. Learned AGP Ms.Bhumi Gandhi submits that learned Patel Deviben Virabhai Expired vs Deputy Collector on 3 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/4214978/
2 reference court justifying in applying market value which is decided by this Court in First Appeal No.1138/2016 and therefore, no error has been committed by the learned reference court and First Appeal is not required to be entertained.

sentences.text: 5. Having considered the submission made by learned advocates for the respective parties, it emerges from the record that the boundary of village Bhapi which is under acquisition and village Vami, on which reliance was placed, is common.

It is also not disputed by learned AGP Ms.Bhumi Gandhi that the decision rendered by the Division Dench of this Court in First Appeal No.701/2017 was accepted and NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2870/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/02/2026 undefined the compensation has been paid to the respective claimants.

It is true that for the same village Vami, another decision was rendered by this Court, prior to the decision rendered in First Appeal No.701/2017 wherein the market value of the land was fixed at the rate of Rs.75/- per sq.mtr.
in which the notification is of the year 1999 however, in the opinion of this Court, the claimants are entitled for the best price as their lands were acquired under the compulsory acquisition.

In that background, it would be more beneficial for the claimants if the decision rendered by the Division Bench of this Court in First Appeal No.701/2017 is applied here, where the date of notification is 28.08.1997.

As in the instant case date of notification having only four months difference i.e 29.04.1997, the claimants would be entitled for the same market value as decided by this Court in First Appeal No.701/2017.

7. Upon perusal of the impugned judgment, it is apparent that the Reference Court has enumerated oral and documentary NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2870/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/02/2026 undefined evidence available on record.

sentences.text: In the present case claimants have relied upon the judgment of village Mahajanpura and village Vami.

Village Mahajanpura is at a distance of 2 km from Vammi and in the judgment of village Mahajanpura market NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2870/2023 JUDGMENT DATED: 03/02/2026 undefined value is determined relying upon the judmgent of village Negla which is confirmed by the Hon'ble Gujarat High Court.
The judgment of village Vami was passed considering the earlier judgment of village Jamda.

Claimants has produced copy of the Judgment of village Vami wide Exhibit 61/1, in which market value of Rs.95.40/- per sq. meters fixed on the date of publication of notification u/s.14 i.e.
29/10/1999.

While in the case of village Nagla market value of Rs.95.40/- per sq.
meter is fixed on the date of publication of notification u/s.4 i.e. 8/8/1999.
Upon considering both the judgments market value in the year 1999 was considered Rs.95.40 per sq. meter.

Ld. Advocate for the claimants has produced previous judgment of same village Vami and therefore in the present references cases market value is determined considering the earlier judgment of LAR No.116/2003 to 131/2003.

Looking to the evidence of the claimant he has stated that notification u/s.
was published on 30/04/1997 but looking to the reference application exh-1 and award passed by LAO notification u/s.4 was published on 28/08/1997.

In section 4(1) of the Act it is provided that the last date of the dates of such publication and the giving of such public notice, being hereinafter referred to as the date of the publication of the notification.
Looking to the award last date of publication is 28/08/1997 and therefore market value on 28/08.1997 of the acquired land is to be determined.
In the present case notification was published on 28/8/1997 while in LAR 116/2003 to 131/2003 date of notification was 29/10/1999 and hence there is time gap of 2 years 2 months 1 day.

Therefore looking to the difference in both notification NEUTRAL CITATION C/FA/2870/2023 JUDGMENT DATED:
03/02/2026 undefined market value can be calculated by 10% decrease per year on Rs.95.40.
So decrease at the rate of 10% of 95.40 for time gap would come to Rs.95.40-9.54=85.86-Rs.8.58=Rs.77.28/- Rs.1.28 = Rs.76.00 per sq. meter.
Therefore in the present case market value on the date of publication of notification i.e. 28/8/1997 comes to Rs.76 per sq. meter.
Hence the claimants are entitled to get Rs.76.00 per sq. mt. as an additional compensation for the acquired land.

Hence I answer issue no.1 in affirmative."
9.

Learned AGP is unable to contest this proposition that where the market value of the land belonging to the same village i.e. Vami being fixed at Rs.95.40 per sq. mtr. and which is accepted by the State then there is no reason to differentiate the market value of similar type of /and of thesame village.
In fact, the Reference Court is justified in arriving at the market value at Rs.77.28 by considering the base price of Rs.95.40 of village Vami where Section 4 notification is dated 29.10.1999.

Thereafter, justifiably has allowed reduction in the market value at the rate of 10% per year considering the fact that Section 4 notification in the present acquisition was published on 28.08.1997, where there is time gap of two years and two months.

The appeals therefore deserve to be and are hereby dismissed.

6. Considering the same, the claimant would be entitled for the market value at the rate of Rs.87.40/- per sq. mtr. i.e. (the market value determined by this Court in First Appeal No.141 of 2026 is Rs.76/-), where the date of Section 4 notification is 29.04.1997 whereas in the instant case,
the date of Section 4 notification is 16.10.1998.
Therefore, giving rise of 10% per year for the first year, it would come to Rs.83.60/- and for another year, 5% rise would be given that would come to Rs.3.80/-.

Accordingly, total amount of Rs.87.40/- would come towards the market value of the acquired land and as the State has accepted the decision rendered by the Division Bench in First Appeal No.701 of 2017, on the basis of which the First Appeal No.141 of 2026 was decided, the respondents are directed to pay the difference amount accordingly.
7. Resultantly, this appeal is allowed.
